newsitem.title: USA: Ohio official hopes pension bond study done in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Ohio official hopes pension bond study done in Q4.

text.p: Ohio's treasurer hopes the state General Assembly will finish by year-end a study designed to help the state decide whether it should sell up $4 billion of pension obligation bonds, his general counsel said Monday.

Raymond Headen, general counsel to the state treasurer, in an interview with Reuters, appeared confident that the proposal was on strong ground, saying "We believe the numbers will speak for themselves."

Headen, along with Treasurer Ken Blackwell, who also serves as the state pension plans' custodian, was in Boston to attend a conference for the National Association of State Auditors, Comptrollers and Treasurers.

By selling $3 billion to $4 billion of taxable pension bonds, Ohio could pay off the pension plans' unfunded liability and capture the market surplus -- estimated at as much as $1 billion -- which then could be rolled into the budget and also used to help lower the state's future pension contributions, Headen explained.

"What we're asking for is just the study in the next several months...to do the study to determine what is the proper valuation of the assets and liabilities in the plans, what are the assumptions that are creating both this market surplus and the unfunded liability."

"And then the last part would be, is it right for the Ohio taxpayer to not take advantage of the market surplus, and if that's a policy decision, to take advantage of the market surplus, then is not the issuance of pension obligation bonds one way of doing that?"

The general counsel added Blackwell last month sent a letter requesting the study to the General Assembly committee handling the issue. "We have gotten positive feedback...that they are going to review the proposal and fund that review," Headen said, adding Gov. George Voinovich also has agreed to look into the proposal.
